exposure: maternal nutrition (poor weight gain, nutritional deficiencies, anemia)
cohort: The study included 1462 maternity women, among whom 53 were diagnosed with confirmed Intrauterine Growth Restriction (IUGR).
finding: The prevalence of IUGR in the hospital was 3.6%, with poor maternal weight gain and pregnancy-induced hypertension identified as major contributing factors.
mod_finding: Among IUGR cases, 58.49% were induced and 58.49% of IUGR babies underwent Caesarean Section.
